summary: Coos County site near Remote, Oregon: a 1928 station report, a tower built by Camp Bradford crews in 1936, and a page entry marked Removed with no date.

facts.status_note: The Forest Lookouts entry ends with the word Removed and gives no date

events.note: Coos County Fire Patrol planned two new lookout stations that year; a station was reported as being built on Thomas Mountain
CCC men from Camp Bradford building four miles of road to Thomas Mountain, February 1936
A June 1936 item calls the Thomas Mountain tower the fourth constructed by Bradford members; an April item had called it the one to be built

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The March 1928 entry says a station was being built on Thomas Mountain. The 1936 items describe a new lookout to be erected and, by June, a completed tower. The page does not reconcile the two, so the built event is dated to 1936 and the 1928 report is kept as 'other'.

notes_for_editor: One source: the Forest Lookouts Oregon page, which quotes Coos Bay Times, Roseburg News-Review and Myrtle Point Herald items (the page spells the last as 'Mrytle'). It names the same towers two ways (Live Oak in April, Libe Oak in June) and the page's 'Dutchmans Butte' and 'Dutchman's butte' differ only by apostrophe. Searches found only California Thomas Mountain lookouts and a Coos Fire Patrol history. A 2012 Oregon lookout report (firelookout.org cr-or-2012.pdf) says lookouts under the Coos Forest Protective Association were not staffed that year, but it does not name Thomas Mountain, so it is not used. Record agency was null and is set from the page's 'Coos County Fire Patrol' heading. Status 'gone' follows the page's Removed entry; no date or cause is given. The story takes the earlier tower names from the April 20, 1936 item, since the June 25, 1936 item spells them 'Libe Oak' and 'Dutchmans Butte'.
